question: Can a Bayesian infinite-width theory derive when a supervised copy head emerges as training-set size increases, and does linear versus softmax attention change the transition from second order plus crossover to first order?

key_findings.claim: The target is a supervised cyclic copy subcircuit, not a complete induction head or language-modeling capability.
key_findings.evidence: Inputs are length-L sequences of i.i.d. uniformly sampled one-hot tokens and each target is the preceding token under periodic boundary conditions. The model is single-layer, single-head, and unmasked, so it omits the previous-token and copy-head composition of a causal two-layer induction circuit.

key_findings.claim: The theory marginalizes a fused attention matrix and readout under an equivalent-kernel approximation to obtain a posterior action over attention patterns.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation takes d_model to infinity, combines the query-key product into W_G, assumes strong regularization with the rich-scaling factor chi, and uses population input averages in the EK data term.

key_findings.claim: Permutation symmetry motivates two collective coordinates: uniform pooling and the shift-by-one copy pattern.
key_findings.evidence: The attention matrix is projected onto order parameters c_1 and c_G for linear attention, with corresponding post-softmax a_1 and a_G coordinates; the dominant posterior is then studied through an effective two-dimensional action.

key_findings.claim: The statement that the two-coordinate reduction has no information loss is stronger than the derivation and experiments support.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 11 is introduced as a representation-theoretically inspired ansatz. Appendix D proves that the summed pseudoinverse must have a three-coefficient symmetry form, but says the coefficients could not be derived analytically and were instead matched to brute-force calculations only for 3 <= L <= 11, 2 <= V <= min(L, 6), and P in {1,...,25}. In the actual L = 25 experiments, linear-attention SGLD coverage falls toward about 80% around the crossover.

anchors.section: 3.3, Claim of reduction without information loss

key_findings.claim: For linear attention, the reduced action has an exact diagonal Z2 symmetry and predicts one genuine second-order transition followed by a copy-pattern crossover rather than a second transition.
key_findings.evidence: The c_1 curvature changes sign at a sample scale proportional to V^2, while the c_G curvature scale is proportional to L^(3/2)V^(1/2). The latter reorganizes an already symmetry-broken phase and Appendix L formalizes it as avoided criticality.

key_findings.claim: For the paper's nominal L = 25, V = 5 parameters, the action locates the linear instability near P = 23 and the crossover near P = 322, but the experimental narrative places them near P = 100 and P = 400.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 gives the numerical scales P*_c1 approximately 23 and P*_cG approximately 322; Section 4 describes departure of c_1 near 100 and copy sharpening beyond roughly 400 while claiming quantitative agreement across all stages. Because the sampled P grid jumps from 20 to 60 to 100 and then from 300 to 400, it cannot localize either empirical boundary finely enough to resolve the first discrepancy or validate exact constants.

key_findings.claim: For softmax attention, row normalization removes the independent pooling coordinate and the reduced action develops two competing minima whose global optimum jumps.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 18-20 express a_1 through a_G and map the softmax pattern back to its preactivation; equating the two minima yields P* scaling approximately as L log^2 L and a claimed O(sqrt(LV)) sample-complexity improvement over linear attention.

key_findings.claim: The experimental softmax order parameter and loss change sharply near P = 300 across separately trained datasets and models.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 compares MAP predictions with Adam and SGLD ensemble averages and shows a jump from near-uniform to copy attention; two-dimensional P-versus-L and P-versus-V loss maps place the theoretical boundary over the observed change.

key_findings.claim: The empirical plots do not establish a first-order thermodynamic singularity at finite model size and chi.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A explicitly says a true phase transition exists only in a large-system limit and finite chi and L soften observables. Experiments fix chi = 30 and d_model = 10,000 and do not vary either to measure rounding, barrier scaling, bimodal weights, hysteresis, latent heat, or susceptibility growth.

anchors.section: Appendix A.1, Definition of a phase transition

key_findings.claim: The apparent abruptness is across models trained with different dataset sizes, not a sudden within-training formation event.
key_findings.evidence: P is the control parameter and each marker comes from a separately trained ensemble at a fixed P. Training trajectories in Figures 6-7 display optimization loss for each setting but do not show one model acquiring the copy capability discontinuously as training time advances.

key_findings.claim: The claim that first-order softmax emergence has no precursor and is intrinsically unpredictable is not demonstrated.
key_findings.evidence: No candidate observable is monitored prospectively, fluctuations and metastable lifetimes are not measured, and the paper's own action predicts the boundary from L, V, priors, and noise. First-order systems can also exhibit nucleation and hysteresis signals, while primary work already predicts induction-head emergence in language-model pretraining.

key_findings.claim: The numerical study uses ten models at each of fourteen P values for each attention mechanism, with a large but narrowly fixed architecture and only 100 test sequences.
The Adam comparison is selected for agreement with the global-MAP object because suboptimal linear-attention runs are filtered after training.
key_findings.evidence: Appendices K and N.1 state that linear Adam runs reaching a local rather than global loss minimum are removed, while softmax runs all converge. The retained count at each P and the effect of filtering on order-parameter means and uncertainty are not reported.

anchors.section: Appendix K, Noncommuting limits and filtering
Appendix N.1, Training Trajectories and Filtering

key_findings.claim: The SGLD results are not accompanied by evidence that the claimed Bayesian stationary distribution was reached or mixed across the competing basins.
key_findings.evidence: Every chain is warm-started from the Adam early-stopping minimum, uses learning rate 5e-10 for at most 15,000 epochs, and is asserted to be initialization-independent only at sufficient time; there are no multiple-chain, effective-sample-size, autocorrelation, basin-switch, or convergence diagnostics.

key_findings.claim: Appendix H contains a sign inconsistency in the advertised derivation of training and test loss from the reduced action.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 294 defines Z proportional to the integral of exp(-S), but Equation 295 prints partial log Z = +<partial S> instead of the required negative expectation, and Equation 297 prints log Z approximately +S* instead of -S*. Equations 301-302 inherit the positive action derivative, so the loss-from-action relation is wrong as printed unless an unstated sign convention or implementation correction is used.

key_findings.claim: The paper supports attention-pattern equivalence for wide factorized Q/K, but its fused experiments do not test the different weight-space prior induced by factorization.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B derives that fused and separately factorized Q/K yield the same Gaussian prior over attention patterns when d_model and d_k are both much larger than L, which fits the nominal d_model = 10,000 and L = 25 regime if d_k is similarly large. Appendix I separately shows that the product matrix's weight-space prior is Frobenius-like only near zero and nuclear-norm-like in its tails; a purely fused Gaussian weight prior is self-consistent when d_k is much larger than d_model and breaks down around d_k comparable to d_model. All experiments train the fused model, so pattern-level asymptotic equivalence is argued but finite-width optimization and regularization equivalence are not tested.

anchors.section: Appendix B, Factorized Q/K attention-pattern prior
Appendix I, Fused versus factorized attention

key_findings.claim: Compute, data, and uncertainty reporting do not support a broad scaling-law claim.
key_findings.evidence: The paper reports about five H100 hours for 'each run of the full ensemble' and 100 H100 hours total, but Appendix N defines fourteen fixed-P ensembles for each of two attention mechanisms. If the quoted five hours applies to each of those 28 ensembles, the literal product is 140 rather than 100 H100 hours; the intended accounting unit is therefore unclear. Dataset redraw policy, retained linear-run counts, confidence intervals, and seed-level values are also absent.

key_findings.claim: The numerical protocol omits prior and decay values needed to reproduce the advertised Bayesian action and SGLD posterior.
key_findings.evidence: The reduced action depends on attention and readout prior scales such as g_W and g_O together with sigma^2. Appendix K states that faithfully realizing distinct Gaussian variances requires a separate weight decay for each parameter family and specifies only g_emb = g_p = 1 symbolically. Appendix N reports chi = 30, sigma^2 = 30, learning rates, and architecture, but not g_Q, g_K or fused g_W, g_O/readout variance, the corresponding per-family decay coefficients, initialization seeds, or the exact data-redraw policy.

anchors.section: Appendix K, Gaussian priors and SGLD

key_findings.claim: No intervention tests whether the inferred order parameters cause copy-head formation or whether changing transition order changes predictability.
key_findings.evidence: The paper varies P, L, V, and attention nonlinearity across separate models and compares theory with outcomes, but it does not manipulate c_1, c_G, barrier height, or softmax temperature while matching data and optimization to test the proposed mechanism.

method.core_idea: Integrate out the weights and outputs of an infinite-width fused attention model, reduce its Bayesian posterior to pooling and copy order parameters using task symmetry, and read transition order and sample complexity from the action's minima.
method.mechanism: Training-set size changes the likelihood-prior balance. Linear attention retains a diagonal sign symmetry, so a curvature change produces continuous pooling order before a lower-scale copy crossover. Softmax normalization removes the independent pooling direction and creates competing minima whose global action exchanges discontinuously.
assumptions: Inputs are i.i.d. uniform one-hot sequences with cyclic supervised copy labels.
Model width is infinite and the equivalent-kernel approximation can replace empirical likelihood structure with population averages.
Strong regularization and large chi L concentrate the posterior sufficiently for a MAP saddle-point treatment.

The asymptotic attention-pattern equivalence derived for d_model, d_k much larger than L is sufficient to transfer fused-model posterior results despite a different factorized weight prior and no factorized experiment.
The two symmetry-selected order parameters capture all materially occupied attention directions.
Finite-time SGLD samples its stationary posterior and filtered Adam minima are a fair optimization comparator.
The unreported attention/readout prior variances and per-family decay coefficients used numerically match the parameters entering the reduced action.

techniques.role: Marginalizes weights and outputs to derive a posterior action over attention patterns.
Projects attention onto uniform-pooling and cyclic-copy collective coordinates.
Classifies continuous, discontinuous, and crossover behavior from action minima and curvatures.
Compares MAP theory with filtered Adam optima and warm-started Langevin samples.
Sweeps P and maps predicted boundaries over sequence length and vocabulary size.

evaluations.setting: Single-layer fused linear attention on cyclic copy, L = 25 and V = 5
evaluations.metric: Pooling/copy order parameters and loss versus P
evaluations.result: Theory predicts a continuous pooling instability near P = 23 and copy crossover near 322; empirical descriptions place the visible changes near 100 and 400.
evaluations.baseline: Filtered Adam ensembles and warm-started SGLD ensembles

evaluations.setting: Single-layer fused softmax attention on the same task
evaluations.metric: Copy order parameter and loss versus P
evaluations.result: The MAP and reported ensemble averages jump near P = 300 from uniform to copy attention.

evaluations.metric: Loss plateaus and theoretical boundary overlays
evaluations.result: The predicted scaling curves visually track the phase regions, but no finite-chi or finite-width scaling and no held-out boundary-error metric are reported.

evaluations.metric: Cosine similarity and projected norm ratio
evaluations.result: Softmax and Adam linear patterns are nearly fully captured, while linear SGLD coverage drops toward 80% around P = 300-600 before recovering.

evaluations.setting: Ten training runs at each P with Adam then SGLD
evaluations.metric: Test loss, convergence, and order-parameter ensemble averages
evaluations.result: The authors label every softmax Adam endpoint the global minimum; linear runs split into loss clusters and the higher-loss cluster is excluded. No independent globality certificate, retained counts, or SGLD mixing diagnostics are reported.
evaluations.baseline: Global MAP minimum of the reduced action

limitations: Author-stated: the analysis is one layer, one head, supervised, unmasked, and uses uniform i.i.d. rather than natural-language tokens.
Author-stated: equivalent-kernel and infinite-width approximations suppress finite-P and finite-d_model corrections.
Author-stated: the genuine induction-head composition in a causal two-layer model remains future work.
Reviewer inference: experiments do not take the large-chi-L limit or measure finite-size rounding needed to establish transition order empirically.

Reviewer inference: Appendix B argues asymptotic attention-pattern equivalence for wide factorized Q/K, but the fused query-key parameterization has a different weight-space prior and is the only model tested.
Reviewer inference: filtered Adam runs and undiagnosed SGLD mixing bias the match to a global-MAP theory.
Reviewer inference: only 100 test sequences, unclear data redraws, absent uncertainty intervals, and ambiguous compute accounting limit the phase diagrams.
Reviewer inference: Appendix H's sign errors make the claimed loss-from-action derivation invalid as printed.
Reviewer inference: g_Q/g_K or fused g_W, g_O/readout variance, family-specific SGLD weight decays, initialization seeds, and retained-run counts are absent from the hyperparameter table.
Reviewer inference: no prospective observable comparison, finite-size transition diagnostic, or within-training emergence experiment supports the claim of precursor-free intrinsic unpredictability.
failure_modes: Finite chi, L, or width can round a nominal action singularity into a smooth crossover.
A factorized query-key model can select different minima through nuclear-norm rather than fused Frobenius regularization.
Adam can remain in a local loss minimum, and filtering it after observing final loss can inflate agreement with global MAP.
Warm-started tiny-step SGLD can stay in the Adam basin within budget and fail to sample posterior basin weights.
Structured or natural token distributions can add order parameters and invalidate the two-coordinate symmetry reduction.
The softmax transition can shift or split under causal masking, multiple heads, residual paths, or a second attention layer.
A cross-P discontinuity can be mistaken for abrupt within-run capability learning.
The printed action-to-loss sign error can invert a derived loss curve if implemented literally.
reusable_insights: A phase diagram over dataset size answers a different question from abrupt circuit formation over optimization time; both axes should be measured explicitly.
Transition-order claims need finite-size rounding, bimodality, hysteresis, susceptibility, and barrier measurements rather than a sharp mean curve alone.
Global-MAP theory should be evaluated both against all optimizer outcomes and against equilibrium samplers with convergence diagnostics.
Separate attention-pattern equivalence from weight-space and optimization equivalence when transferring a fused QK theory to factorized Transformer attention.
Symmetry-derived order parameters are most convincing when residual subspace coverage and coefficient derivations are validated at the actual experimental scale.
Claims of unpredictability require a prospective observable tournament; absence of an order-parameter precursor is not absence of all predictive information.
open_questions: Does the softmax boundary remain first order under causal masking, factorized Q/K, two layers, residual connections, and natural token statistics?
Do finite-chi and finite-width experiments show the rounding, bimodality, switching time, and hysteresis predicted for a first-order transition?
Can multiple independent SGLD chains mix between the two minima and recover their posterior weights without Adam warm starts?
How many linear Adam runs are filtered at each P, and does including them falsify the claimed quantitative agreement?
Can past-only spectral, loss-landscape, or attention-fluctuation signals forecast the copy transition despite the absence of a continuous softmax order-parameter precursor?
Does correcting Appendix H's signs reproduce every plotted loss surface and boundary?
What exact g_Q, g_K or fused g_W, g_O/readout variance, and per-family SGLD decay values generated the reported posterior curves?
Does a matched softmax-temperature or barrier-height intervention move the boundary and predictability in the direction implied by the reduced action?

competitive_landscape.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
competitive_landscape.difference: Olsson et al. identify induction heads, their abrupt formation, and their relationship to in-context learning in causal multi-layer language models; the present paper isolates only the first-layer copy subcircuit in a supervised cyclic one-layer task.

competitive_landscape.title: The mechanistic basis of data dependence and abrupt learning in an in-context classification task
competitive_landscape.difference: Reddy analyzes data-dependent abrupt learning through optimization-time competition and explicitly identifies progress measures that precede in-context learning. The present paper gives an equilibrium Bayesian action as dataset size varies, so Reddy is both a dynamics comparator and direct prior evidence against a broad no-precursor claim.

competitive_landscape.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation
competitive_landscape.difference: Singh et al. intervene on and decompose the prerequisites for induction-head formation in multi-layer models; the present work predicts a copy-order boundary but performs no causal circuit intervention.

competitive_landscape.title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structure with Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: Nichani et al. prove that gradient descent in a causal two-layer Transformer recovers latent causal graphs, with Markov-chain induction heads as a special case. The present model is unmasked and one-layer and replaces training dynamics with a posterior equilibrium calculation over a supervised cyclic-copy task.

competitive_landscape.title: Unveiling Induction Heads: Provable Training Dynamics and Feature Learning in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. give optimization-time feature-learning guarantees for induction heads, whereas the present paper gives equilibrium sample-complexity transitions for a fused copy head and does not prove Adam or SGLD dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Emergence of Induction Heads for In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Musat et al. prove that modified two-layer Transformer training stays in a 19-dimensional subspace, empirically localize emergence to three dimensions, and derive quadratic context-length scaling of emergence time. The present paper instead studies an equilibrium dataset-size boundary for a single fused copy subcircuit and does not analyze optimization time.

competitive_landscape.title: Predicting the Emergence of Induction Heads in Language Model Pretraining
competitive_landscape.difference: Aoyama et al. explicitly predict induction-head emergence during language-model pretraining, directly limiting the broad claim that softmax copy emergence is intrinsically unpredictable from observables.

competitive_landscape.title: Linear attention is (maybe) all you need (to understand transformer optimization)
competitive_landscape.difference: Ahn et al. use shallow linearized Transformers to reproduce and analyze optimization phenomena in in-context regression. The present paper uses linear attention as a symmetry-preserving Bayesian comparator for a copy task and focuses on dataset-size equilibrium phase order rather than gradient-descent convergence.

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Regularization of Gradient Flow on One-Layer Softmax Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Sheen et al. show nuclear-norm implicit regularization for separately trained key and query matrices, contrasting it with Frobenius regularization of a combined matrix. The present paper derives asymptotic attention-pattern equivalence for wide factorized Q/K but tests only the fused model, so it does not establish equivalent finite-width optimization or weight-prior selection.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Capabilities Arise Randomly from Learning Sparse Attention Patterns
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct post-submission competitor on stochastic within-training attention-pattern emergence.
competitive_landscape.difference: Baherwani et al. link abrupt capabilities to the stochastic learning of sparse task-relevant attention patterns in synthetic Transformers and Pythia, varying context length, sparsity, head count, head dimension, and alternative mixers. The present paper offers an analytic equilibrium boundary for a supervised copy pattern but does not measure stochastic within-training arrival, architecture controls, or natural-model capabilities.

competitive_landscape.title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct current competitor on first-order-style emergence kinetics, precursors, and intervention.
competitive_landscape.difference: Dong models circuit formation as a driven rare event, reports a prospective precursor that dates held-out capability arrival, and intervenes on data mixture and query-key slices in models up to 1.4B parameters. The present paper derives a cleaner exact posterior boundary for a single fused copy head, but its intrinsic-unpredictability claim is directly limited by this later primary evidence and it has no kinetic or causal test.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a first-principles Bayesian theory of copy-head emergence that reduces the attention posterior without information loss, predicts linear attention's second-order transition and crossover, predicts softmax's first-order jump and improved sample complexity, and implies that the latter has no precursor and is intrinsically unpredictable.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The action and symmetry analysis give explicit, testable boundaries and distinguish one true linear transition from an avoided second one. Ten-model fused-attention ensembles and P-L-V phase maps broadly follow the predicted topology, while projection coverage supports the order parameters away from linear SGLD's crossover region. The empirical setup, however, fixes the asymptotic parameters, filters linear Adam failures, supplies no SGLD mixing diagnostics, omits several prior/decay values needed to reproduce the action, and contains a sign error in the action-to-loss appendix.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is the unified Bayesian reduced-action comparison of linear and softmax copy attention, including explicit sample-complexity scalings and a careful theoretical distinction between symmetry breaking and crossover. Priority does not extend to induction-head discovery, abrupt in-context learning, provable induction dynamics, factorized softmax regularization, or prediction of induction-head emergence. Reddy reports precursor progress measures, Aoyama predicts formation from data and throughput statistics, Baherwani et al. study stochastic within-training sparse-pattern arrival, and Dong reports a prospective circuit precursor and interventions, so intrinsic unpredictability is not a defensible general novelty claim. Claims of loss derivation, lossless reduction, empirical first-order proof, and transfer to causal induction heads remain too broad until the sign chain is corrected, the actual L/V regime is derived rather than small-scale numerically matched, finite-size scaling and unfiltered optimizer outcomes are reported, and causal factorized experiments are run.

reviewer_notes: Independent second pass over all 54 pages of the byte-pinned arXiv v1 PDF and extracted text, including the complete main text, references, all equations and phase diagrams, proofs and derivations, coverage analysis, factorized-prior discussion, field-theory appendix, numerical protocol, and every panel in Figures 1-7. The current export.arxiv.org PDF was downloaded again on 2026-08-23 and matched SHA-256 aec2ee6f2d20fe9b8c48420d36b42cc539fb39e2d011735e9fbf2d7ad27743b6 exactly. Equation 295 and Equation 297 were checked at high resolution against Equation 294's exp(-S) definition; the sign failure is confined to the advertised action-to-loss chain rather than extrapolated to the independently minimized action. The audit also repaired the fused/factorized comparison by separating pattern-level wide-limit equivalence from weight-prior and optimization equivalence, and it identified missing prior/decay values. Eleven direct current primary records were rechecked at exact official arXiv revisions, including post-submission evidence on sparse-attention emergence and predictive circuit kinetics. Residual uncertainty remains about finite-size transition order, sampler mixing, filtered runs, unreleased seed-level values, and whether the unreported implementation corrected the printed signs.
